services.name: Speech and language therapy
services.title: Speech Therapy in Greater Noida | Aasha
services.answer: Aasha provides individualised speech and language therapy in Gamma 2, Greater Noida, supporting understanding, expression, articulation and social communication—including gesture, pictures and other communication methods, not speech alone.
services.heading: Communication in everyday life
areas: Understanding spoken language and following everyday conversations
Expressing needs, choices and ideas using speech or other communication methods
Articulation and speech clarity
Pre-linguistic skills such as pointing, gestures, turn-taking and joint attention in early play
Social communication during play, family routines and school activities
services.prepare: Share what your child currently communicates, which languages are used at home and school, and situations where communication is difficult. Note any words or gestures your child used before but no longer uses—loss of established communication deserves prompt mention rather than waiting for the appointment. Previous reports and teacher observations help the team understand everyday needs.
services.process: The team identifies communication priorities with the family and plans individualised activities. Where speech is limited or inconsistent, augmentative and alternative communication—gestures, picture supports or devices—may be introduced; usable communication is valued over forced speech. Parent guidance connects session goals with home routines, including how to respond to every communication attempt, not only spoken words.

faq.question: Does speech therapy focus only on pronunciation?
faq.answer: No. Aasha’s speech and language service also considers understanding language, expressing needs and ideas, pre-linguistic skills such as pointing and gesture, social communication and alternative communication methods where appropriate. Support does not wait until a child can speak; it starts from how the child communicates today.

services.name: Occupational therapy
services.title: Occupational Therapy in Greater Noida | Aasha
services.answer: Aasha offers occupational therapy for children in Gamma 2, Greater Noida, focusing on fine motor skills, sensory responses, visual-motor coordination, play and everyday independence.
services.heading: Participation, comfort and independence
areas: Fine motor activities and hand skills
Sensory responses that affect participation—what a child finds overwhelming or actively seeks
Visual-motor coordination during play and learning
Gross motor confidence, posture and movement across familiar environments
Activities of daily living and age-appropriate independence
services.prepare: Describe routines your child finds easy or difficult, including play, school tasks and daily self-care. Note reactions to noise, touch, clothing tags, food textures or busy places, and what calms or unsettles your child. Bring earlier therapy or developmental reports if available.
services.process: An individualised plan connects therapy activities with practical goals agreed with the family. Rather than trying to extinguish harmless repetitive movement, the team looks at what a child gains from it—regulation, predictability or enjoyment—and builds communication and participation around genuine needs. Occupational therapy can be coordinated with speech therapy, special education or behavioural support when those services are relevant.

faq.question: How are occupational therapy goals chosen?
faq.answer: Goals come from the child’s assessment, daily routines, strengths and family priorities—not from making a child look typical. Harmless self-communication or movement is not automatically a target to remove. Progress is reviewed so the plan responds to changing needs.

services.name: Special education and learning support
services.title: Special Education in Greater Noida | Aasha
services.answer: Aasha provides individualised special education and academic remediation in Greater Noida for children with learning difficulties, including specific learning disabilities such as dyslexia, dysgraphia and dyscalculia.
services.heading: Learning support built around the child
areas: Reading and literacy needs, including dyslexia
Writing needs, including dysgraphia
Mathematics needs, including dyscalculia
Learning gaps, classroom participation and school-support planning
Adapting instruction for children whose profile is uneven—strong understanding alongside slow written output
services.prepare: Bring school feedback, examples of schoolwork and previous assessments if available. Share which tasks cause frustration, what your child enjoys learning and the support already tried at home or school. A child who understands verbally but struggles on paper presents a different plan from one with broad difficulty, so concrete examples matter more than labels.
services.process: Assessment findings inform individualised learning goals and academic remediation. Sessions build on the child’s actual strengths—special interests, visual reasoning or spoken knowledge—rather than working only on weaknesses, and accommodations such as extra time or alternative ways to demonstrate learning can be discussed. The team can explain practical home and classroom support with families and coordinate with schools with family consent.

faq.question: Is special education the same as a learning-disability assessment?
faq.answer: No. Assessment explores the child’s learning profile and support needs; special education provides individualised learning support. Difficulty copying from a board or slow handwriting may have several explanations—the team can explain whether an assessment would help plan the next step.

services.name: ABA and behavioural support
services.title: Child Behavioural Support & ABA | Aasha Greater Noida
services.answer: Aasha offers individualised ABA-informed and behavioural support in Greater Noida for communication, emotional regulation, positive social participation and everyday life skills—planned around each child rather than a fixed programme.
services.heading: Understanding behaviour in context
areas: Communication and functional life skills
Emotional regulation and participation in routines
Challenging behaviours that affect home or school life
Positive social interaction and family support
services.prepare: Describe what happens before, during and after a difficult situation, what your child may be communicating and what helps them feel comfortable. Include relevant health, communication and sensory information—pain, constipation, poor sleep or an inability to ask for help can look like behaviour. Note what has already helped, however briefly.
services.process: The team discusses assessment findings and goals with the family before planning behavioural interventions. Support focuses on teaching useful communication and adjusting environments so difficult behaviour is less necessary, rather than simply suppressing harmless movements or forcing eye contact. Interventions are coordinated with other services when appropriate, and goals and progress are reviewed with parents; a plan that increases distress is reconsidered instead of blamed on the child.

faq.question: Does every child need the same behavioural programme?
faq.answer: No. Aasha plans support around each child’s assessment, communication, sensory needs and family priorities. Behaviour is treated as information about an unmet need, not defiance. The team explains the proposed approach and reviews the plan over time.

services.name: Child developmental and psychological assessments
services.title: Child Developmental Assessment | Aasha Greater Noida
services.answer: Dr. Sana Firdos leads Aasha’s child developmental and psychological assessments in Greater Noida, using cognitive, behavioural and developmental evaluations to guide support—not a single test that decides a child’s future.
services.heading: Clarity before an intervention plan
areas: Developmental strengths and areas needing support
Cognitive and IQ assessment where relevant
Behavioural and emotional concerns
Diagnostic questions about learning, attention and development
Autism and ADHD evaluation, including observations across settings and structured tools where appropriate
services.prepare: Bring developmental and medical history, earlier reports, school feedback and the questions you want the assessment to address. Note early communication signs—pointing, gestures, first words—and any loss of skills previously used consistently, since timing shapes the pathway. The team confirms relevant tools, sessions and report arrangements before booking.
services.process: Dr. Sana Firdos, Clinical Psychologist and Head of Assessments, leads the assessment pathway. Findings inform an individualised therapy roadmap with Dr. Anita Sharma’s clinical oversight. The selection of tests depends on the referral question; results are explained as a profile of strengths and needs rather than a single number, and assessment can proceed even when families begin without a diagnosis or a clear label.

faq.question: Will every child receive the same tests?
faq.answer: No. The assessment plan depends on the child’s age, developmental history, presenting concerns and referral question. Tools answer different questions—a screening checklist, a diagnostic evaluation and a functional assessment are not interchangeable. The team confirms the scope and explains the findings with the family.

services.name: Child psychiatric consultation
services.title: Child Psychiatric Consultation | Aasha Greater Noida
services.answer: Consult Dr. Anita Sharma at Aasha in Greater Noida for childhood psychiatric and neurodevelopmental concerns, with coordinated psychological assessment and therapy planning—begin with a concern, not necessarily a diagnosis.
services.heading: A coordinated starting point for families
areas: Developmental, behavioural and emotional concerns
Attention and school-related difficulties
Childhood psychiatric and neurodevelopmental conditions, including autism, ADHD and co-occurring anxiety or mood concerns
Coordination of medical, psychological and therapy goals
services.prepare: Share your main concerns, developmental and medical history, any current medicines, previous reports and school observations. You can begin with a concern even if your child has not received a diagnosis. Mention anything that changed quickly—new aggression, lost skills, poor sleep or reduced awareness—so the team can judge urgency before the appointment.
services.process: Dr. Anita Sharma, Consultant Psychiatrist and Clinical Director, reviews the child’s needs and discusses next steps with the family. These may include psychological assessment, therapy planning, follow-up or referral, depending on the clinical evaluation. Where medicine is considered, it forms part of a broader plan with agreed goals and monitoring; treatment decisions are explained rather than presented as fixed protocols.

faq.question: Do we need a diagnosis before booking?
faq.answer: No. Families can begin by describing their concerns. The consultation helps clarify which assessment, intervention or further referral may be appropriate—and whether any feature needs faster medical attention.

faqs.question: Where is Aasha Early Intervention Centre?
faqs.answer: Aasha is at J-123, J Block, Gamma 2, Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh 201310. Call +91 96678 63295 for appointment coordination and directions.

faqs.question: What are Aasha’s clinic hours?
faqs.answer: Aasha is open Monday to Saturday from 12:00 PM to 8:00 PM and is closed on Sunday. Contact the coordination team to arrange an appointment.

faqs.question: What child development services does Aasha provide?
faqs.answer: Aasha provides child psychiatric consultation, clinical psychological and developmental assessments, speech and language therapy, occupational therapy, special education, and ABA and behavioural support. The mix of services is planned for each child.

faqs.question: Who leads care and assessments at Aasha?
faqs.answer: Dr. Anita Sharma is Consultant Psychiatrist and Clinical Director. Dr. Sana Firdos is Clinical Psychologist and Head of Assessments.

faqs.question: How do I book a child assessment at Aasha?
faqs.answer: Call +91 96678 63295 or use the website’s appointment request form. Share your child’s main concerns and any earlier reports so the coordination team can help arrange the appropriate first step.

faqs.question: How is Aasha related to the services on the Mind Grace website?
faqs.answer: All child-related care on this website comes under Aasha Child Development & Early Intervention Centre. Adult care and academic training continue under Mind Grace.

faqs.question: My child lost words or skills they used before. Is that urgent?
faqs.answer: Loss of an established skill deserves prompt medical discussion—contact your paediatrician or Aasha and say explicitly that skills have been lost. If a child is difficult to wake, has breathing difficulty, sudden weakness or a prolonged seizure, seek emergency care immediately rather than waiting for a developmental appointment.

faqs.question: Does Aasha recommend special diets, supplements or biomedical protocols for autism?
faqs.answer: No. Aasha focuses on assessment, therapy and coordinated medical care. Elimination diets, supplement stacks or tests marketed as autism treatments should be discussed with your clinician first; restriction without a specific medical reason can harm nutrition, and unexplained worsening should be assessed rather than called detoxification.

faqs.question: Can my child start therapy before receiving a diagnosis?
faqs.answer: Often yes. Support planning can begin from observed needs—communication, sensory comfort, learning or regulation—while assessment continues. A diagnosis may help explain needs and access services, but families do not need to wait for one to start a practical conversation about support.
